title: Why Is Netflix Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity? | NFLX Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names and figures in places
summary: Parkevtate asks whether Netflix, trading below $60 near its 52-week low, is a falling knife or a generational buying opportunity. He reviews management's latest update: the strategy of best-in-class entertainment with global discovery, distribution and monetisation is mostly working — over 300 million paying subscribers, the highest average revenue per user and the industry's lowest churn, which improved again in Q3 despite price rises. The concern is engagement: it is barely growing as viewers shift to short-form content and YouTube gains share with its free ad-supported service, while rivals now offer more live sports. Netflix is leaning into live events and exploring creator and third-party content, though its pay-for-content model does not map neatly onto YouTube's revenue-share model. He argues management has communicated this poorly and should consider a free ad-supported tier. On valuation, forward P/E of 15.8 is near the lowest in company history, and his revised DCF fair value is $98 versus ~$59. NFLX is his largest position and a top-10 buy; he may add more before next earnings. Call: NFLX BUY reiterated at ~$59, DCF $98 (cut from $120 on 2 Nov).
